scope: EOS R5 full RAW CR3 metadata first, associated XMP and stored previews; secondary variants separate. Native declared read/preview slice and scoped private evidence in docs/reader. Whole capability rows remain specified; no full-format/tag-family parity or writes claimed.

variants.notes: User-selected losslessly compressed full RAW. Eight private files characterized at firmware 2.2.1; stored mode observations and coverage limits in docs/corpus-baseline. No native or general variant support claim.
Association and conflict policy required; never infer embedded CR3 write support from sidecar support.
Separate evidence; not a gate for the first full-RAW read milestone.
User has not stated use; additional sensor data preservation remains a separate gate.

mappings.target: Explicit coverage levels and omission reporting; normal CR3 inspection includes its CTMD contract.
mappings.acceptance: Compare shallow/complete scans and declare skipped samples or unknown blocks; no speed mode silently claims complete privacy inspection.

mappings.target: files rename/move/copy/set-times previews RAW and XMP effects together.
mappings.acceptance: Collision, ordering, platform timestamp limits and paired rollback/recovery have named outcomes.

mappings.target: time inspect/set/shift distinguishes elapsed time, calendar changes and offsets.
mappings.acceptance: No host timezone is invented for zone-less EXIF; RAW/sidecar targets and CTMD constraints are visible.

mappings.target: geo tag previews track matching, interpolation, clock drift and destination.
mappings.acceptance: Known samples, time gaps, UTC/offset differences and multiple synchronization points have expected results.

mappings.target: Record geographic lookup separately from GPS track matching; auxiliary databases and exact outputs need a later specification.
mappings.acceptance: Keep offline/default privacy and database provenance explicit; no bundled database or network service is selected here.

mappings.target: Preview/apply, backup restore/prune and explicit output policy share a recovery contract.
mappings.acceptance: Hardlinks, permissions, timestamps, stale inputs and failure between backup/replacement are tested; defaults need not mimic ExifTool.

mappings.target: validate and diagnostic views provide stable issue codes; repairs and ignored-errors policies require explicit requests.
mappings.acceptance: No broad ignore-errors flag bypasses preservation gates; malformed inputs remain bounded and explainable.

mappings.target: batch and persistent requests use explicit IDs/framing and isolate queued mutations.
mappings.acceptance: Completion and success are separate; stdout/stderr framing, EOF, cancellation and option lifetime have tests.

mappings.target: Typed request/JSON manifests and NUL path lists avoid shell quoting ambiguities.
mappings.acceptance: Paths with Unicode, newlines, leading hyphens and reserved help words reach the intended file exactly.

mappings.target: Stable native issue and exit codes distinguish partial failure, invalid invocation, stale plan, verification and cancellation.
mappings.acceptance: Machine stdout remains parseable; warnings and deliberate selection exclusions have documented status behavior.

mappings.target: Preserve RAW transformation/custom-tag use cases while choosing a deliberate execution/trust boundary later.
mappings.acceptance: No implicit arbitrary-code execution; unsupported constructs get migration guidance and never silently change meaning.

mappings.target: Independent read engine returns structured results reusable across selections without terminal dependency.
mappings.acceptance: Repeated queries do not reparse unnecessarily or mutate source state; read limits and diagnostics remain attributable.

mappings.target: A language-independent occurrence model exposes identity, groups, raw/rational/normalized/display values and definitions.
mappings.acceptance: Same-name occurrences and exact values survive across retrievals; public calling conventions remain undecided.

mappings.target: Explicit edit plan/request state instead of accidentally retained writes across requests.
mappings.acceptance: Define reset/copy/reuse and error outcomes; every apply rechecks content identity and preservation gates.

mappings.target: Build a typed transfer plan with occurrence/location mappings and source fingerprints.
mappings.acceptance: Copied source changes invalidate a saved plan; missing and unsupported mappings are visible.

mappings.target: Registry discovery is distinct from content-based detection and per-file write eligibility.
mappings.acceptance: A filename-derived type hint or global tag list cannot grant a write capability.

mappings.target: Classify relevant option families as read coverage, presentation, typing, performance or mutation policy; exhaustive option audit remains open.
mappings.acceptance: Every adopted option has scope/lifetime/default tests; CR3 UTC and padding behavior receive dedicated cases.

gaps.subject: EOS R5 fixture observations
gaps.closesWhen: Initial private observations from #0013 are documented in docs/corpus-baseline. Remaining coverage: A provenance-approved full RAW corpus records camera/firmware/mode, discovered structures, optional-tag presence and source hashes.
gaps.blocks: Generalizing the eight observed files to other capture settings, firmware, layouts or optional-field coverage.

gaps.subject: Camera mode and damaged-file discrimination
gaps.closesWhen: Cross-check brand, Canon model, Quality and structural clues on full RAW/C-RAW/DPRAW and negative CRM/other-camera cases; record ambiguity rules.
gaps.blocks: Automatic mode identification and variants inheriting one another's support.

gaps.subject: Tag-level and mutation-depth expansion
gaps.closesWhen: Expand representative families into occurrence/tag/location rows; audit insertion/deletion flags, defaults and all relevant maker-note subtables without copying upstream tables.
gaps.blocks: Exhaustive tag-count claims or broad all-tags-writable claims.

gaps.subject: Saved plans and preservation oracle
gaps.closesWhen: The proposed contract is recorded in docs/write-safety. Demonstrate guarded per-file publication, partial-pair outcomes, sensor/reference/calibration/opaque preservation, properties and interruption recovery on declared storage/writer profiles before enabling writes.

gaps.subject: Metadata interpretation and conversion evidence
gaps.closesWhen: Initial private observations from #0013 are documented in docs/corpus-baseline. Remaining coverage: The proposed model contract is recorded in docs/metadata-model. Exercise its identity, exact value, XMP, encoding, and time rules against real fixtures and per-tag oracle observations before claiming runtime equivalence.
gaps.blocks: Runtime lossless JSON/import/copy and per-tag interpretation claims; the language-independent model specification is delivered by card #0004.

gaps.subject: Legacy argument and API completeness
gaps.closesWhen: The surveyed surface ledger and migration/trust recommendations are in docs/legacy-compatibility. Close LG-001/LG-002/LG-003/LG-005/LG-006 through exhaustive option/API/ordering cases, accepted differences and actual reference/native evidence before claiming full or drop-in parity.

gaps.subject: Preview variants and nested metadata
gaps.closesWhen: Initial private observations from #0013 are documented in docs/corpus-baseline. Remaining coverage: Enumerate THMB, PRVW and JPEG-track assets per full RAW fixture; prove bytes and nested metadata coverage; audit any replacement path separately.
gaps.blocks: All-previews claims, nested privacy completeness, or preview replacement.

gaps.subject: Repeatable runtime reference
gaps.closesWhen: The initial reference has been acquired, hashed and run in controlled configuration on #0013; see docs/corpus-baseline. Reproduce on another environment and extend actual records to each additional claimed operation.
gaps.blocks: Claims of repeatability beyond the recorded environment and operations; any native parity percentage.

gaps.subject: Privacy and sidecar synchronization policy
gaps.closesWhen: The proposed destination, residual-data, pairing-outcome and rendering-critical retention rules are recorded in docs/write-safety. Specify exact pairing/mappings and per-profile field catalogs, then verify removal, residual/uninspectable coverage and synchronization on lawful fixtures. Logical removal never proves secure erasure.
gaps.blocks: Secure-erasure/anonymization claims or silent RAW/sidecar synchronization.

gaps.subject: Secondary and later format breadth
gaps.closesWhen: Scope and collect independent evidence for C-RAW/DPRAW, other Canon cameras and later RAW families before adding their capabilities.
gaps.blocks: Using the initial EOS R5 full RAW results as universal RAW support.

gaps.subject: Asset licensing and provenance
gaps.closesWhen: The initial 35 private fixtures and four reference-tool components have scoped reviews on #0013; see docs/corpus-baseline. Apply the provenance policy to every new import and independently authorize any public distribution. No blanket reuse grant is implied.
gaps.blocks: Redistribution of upstream assets or personal sample media.

gaps.subject: CLI workflows and large-input boundaries
gaps.closesWhen: CLI walkthroughs, request/result schemas, pure filter and persistent-session proposals are recorded. Complete saved-plan and session-output schemas, advanced mappings and remaining LG-001–006 specifications on #0015; use the #0008 performance protocol to establish measured limits on #0016 and later prove actual CLI/help/menu/transport behavior.
gaps.blocks: Claiming the proposed CLI surface is finalized or implemented.
